body:
Slice 6 of T-MANIFEST-FOREST. Implements §9.1–9.3 of `docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md`, which are normative and already authored — read them before starting; this ticket does not restate them, it scopes and verifies them.

## Problem

`packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/manifest.mjs` is the gate's single committed-tree reader for evidence. It has **zero** forest awareness: `grep -cE 'manifest\.d|segment|anchor' packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/manifest.mjs` returns 0. Its exported surface is `committedManifestAtHead`, `baseManifestBytes`, `assertAppendOnly`, `manifestRawLines`, `manifestLines`, `validateMigrationEvidence`, and every one of them addresses `.adlc/manifest.jsonl` alone. The sole call site is `packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs` (~lines 294–302).

Slices 1–4 shipped the forest read layer, the cross-model reader, the segment writer, and greenfield activation. So a repo can already be in forest mode, and once it is, **new evidence is written to `.adlc/manifest.d/*.jsonl` — files this gate does not look at.** The append-only protection that `assertAppendOnly` provides for the root simply does not exist for segments: a PR can rewrite, truncate, reorder, or delete any committed segment file and CI will not notice.

That is the security-relevant gap, and it is why this slice must land BEFORE the migration ceremony (slice 5) and before this repository cuts over. Cutting over first would move all new evidence into the unguarded path — trading a merge-conflict annoyance for the loss of the gate's tamper-evidence in PRs.

Secondary, lower-severity gap: today's root rule is only the byte-prefix check, so ANY appended entries pass. §9.1 tightens this to a permitted-append set and freezes the root byte-identical once base is cutover.

## What to build

Implement §9.1, §9.2, and §9.3 in the existing single reader. Keep the existing hardening — it was argued once per reader deliberately and must be reused, not reimplemented:

- Pin HEAD to one immutable sha and resolve every lookup against it (the #314 round-7 TOCTOU fix).
- Guard the `.adlc` ancestor: it must be a real tree (mode `040000`), never a symlink or submodule.
- Read blobs by the immutable hash from the same `ls-tree` row, never `git show HEAD:path`.
- Every segment file gets the same mode/type check the root gets today: regular blob, `100644`, never a symlink or submodule. A symlinked segment is exactly the smuggling vector the root check exists to stop, and there will now be many more files to point at.
- Fail closed on any `git` non-zero status (`fail(...)`, not silent skip).
- Byte-level comparisons stay byte-level. utf8 decoding is non-injective, so no prefix check may run on decoded text.

### §9.1 Root

- Base root NOT cutover: HEAD root must still have base root as a byte prefix, and the only permitted appended entries are a valid migration-evidence set (existing `validateMigrationEvidence` behavior, unchanged) **or** a valid seal+cutover set per §4.5–4.6, chain-verified over actual raw lines exactly as migration evidence is today.
- Base root IS cutover (last base entry has `gate === 'manifest-cutover'`): HEAD root must be **byte-identical** to base. This is what freezes the root.
- Seal and cutover entries must structurally carry `sigVersion: 2` and a `sig` field. rails-guard holds no key, so it checks **presence only** — do not attempt signature verification here, and do not treat presence as proof of validity. The spec is explicit that spoofing is contained rather than prevented: a keyless author can append a structurally valid fake cutover, but its absent-or-invalid signature makes every keyed reader fail the forest closed, so the spoof denies the spoofer.

### §9.2 Existing segments

Every segment file present at base must have its base bytes as a byte prefix of its HEAD bytes — per-file append-only, the direct generalization of `assertAppendOnly`. Deleting or renaming a base-committed segment file in a PR must deny.

### §9.3 New segments

Every segment file present at HEAD but not at base must:

- match the §4.2 filename grammar,
- be a regular blob (mode/type checked as the root is today),
- parse and chain-verify internally over raw lines,
- carry an anchor that resolves — with a matching `lineHash`, cycle-checked — within the **HEAD** forest, whose anchored-to segment is itself valid under §9.1–9.3.

Resolving at HEAD rather than base is deliberate: a PR may legitimately mint a second segment anchored to one it added itself. History pinning comes from §9.1/§9.2, not from where anchors point.

`anchor: null` is permitted whenever the **base tree contains no root** — regardless of how many other segments the base tree already has. This is deliberately NOT "no root and no segments": two branches forked from the same root-less state each mint an independent `anchor: null` segment (§7.1) without seeing each other, and whichever merges second must not be denied merely because the first is now part of base. Its signed anchor cannot be repointed after the fact without invalidating the signature (§4.4), and §5's forest model is explicitly a forest of trees rooted in the root segment **or** in `anchor: null` segments, plural.

### §9.4

`validateMigrationEvidence` retains its current behavior for the ticket-store migration and gains the seal+cutover validation of §9.1. Trusted-base resolution, symlink/submodule ancestor guards, and blob-hash pinned reads are reused unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

Each is a test in `packages/rails-guard/test/`, run with `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/<file>` and covered by `npm test`. Write each test first and observe it FAIL before implementing (the mutation gate will otherwise flag the guard as uncovered).

1. **A modified committed segment denies.** A fixture repo where base has `.adlc/manifest.d/<seg>.jsonl` and HEAD rewrites a byte inside the base region → deny. Currently PASSES silently; this is the headline regression.
2. **A truncated committed segment denies.** HEAD version is shorter than base → deny.
3. **A deleted committed segment denies.** Present at base, absent at HEAD → deny.
4. **A renamed committed segment denies.** Present at base under one grammar-valid name, absent at HEAD under that name → deny (the add of the new name is separately subject to AC7–AC9).
5. **A pure append to a committed segment passes.** Base bytes are a byte prefix of HEAD bytes → allowed.
6. **A symlinked segment denies.** A segment committed as a symlink, and as a submodule → deny for both, mirroring the root's mode/type rule.
7. **A new segment with a resolving anchor passes**, including the case where it anchors to another segment added in the same PR.
8. **A new segment whose anchor does not resolve denies.** Anchor names a segment/seq that exists nowhere in the HEAD forest → deny.
9. **A new segment whose anchor resolves but whose `lineHash` does not match denies.**
10. **An anchor cycle denies.** Two new segments anchored to each other → deny, and the check terminates (a test that hangs fails this ticket).
11. **A new segment that does not chain-verify internally denies.**
12. **A new segment whose filename violates the §4.2 grammar denies.**
13. **`anchor: null` is permitted when the base tree has no root**, including when base already contains other segments (the §7.1 two-branch case). Assert BOTH sub-cases; the second is the one a narrower reading gets wrong.
14. **`anchor: null` denies when the base tree HAS a root.**
15. **Root frozen after cutover.** Base root ends in `manifest-cutover`, HEAD root differs by even one appended byte → deny. And byte-identical → pass.
16. **A valid seal+cutover append passes** when base root is not cutover, chain-verified over raw lines.
17. **An appended region containing any cutover or seal entry that is not a valid seal+cutover set denies.** The original wording denied EVERY unrelated append, which contradicts spec §11 (single-file repos keep exact current behavior indefinitely — ordinary evidence appends in PRs are that behavior) and was disproven by the entrypoint suite during the build. Ordinary appends remain legal until the base root is cutover; strictness triggers on the presence of cutover/seal-shaped entries in the appended region.
18. **Seal/cutover entries missing `sig` or `sigVersion: 2` deny.**
19. **Existing behavior is unchanged for a segment-free repo.** The current ticket-store migration-evidence tests and append-only tests pass untouched. A repo with no `.adlc/manifest.d/` must produce byte-for-byte the same verdicts as before this change — assert with the existing test files unmodified.
20. **Operational failures fail closed.** A `git` invocation returning non-zero during segment enumeration or blob read causes `fail(...)`, not a skipped check.
21. **Full suite green:** `npm test` exits 0.

## Trust-root tier

`packages/rails-guard/**` is an enforcement package and a rails deny-path. P5 prosecution requires a distinct-provider `cross-model-review` approve bound to the reviewed revision before merge — a clean same-model P5 is not sufficient and `adlc prosecute --base <ref>` will exit 2 until it is recorded.

## Out of scope

- The migration ceremony itself (`adlc gate-manifest migrate`) — T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 5.
- Migrating this repository's manifest — T-MANIFEST-FOREST-MIGRATE, which this ticket blocks.
- Making `repair-chain` per-segment (slice 7) and the docs/doctor work (slice 8).
- Any change to signing, to `packages/gate-manifest`, or to the forest read layer.
title: rails-guard CI must guard the manifest forest: root cutover rules, per-segment append-only, and new-segment anchor validation (T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 6)
